An append-only event log needs the weaker property \u2014 idempotent writers \u2014 because it must tolerate side effects (writing events) while bounding them under retry.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110 does not formally state that safe methods are a subset of idempotent methods, the hierarchy claim fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log uses a monotonically increasing sequence number that makes raw append naturally idempotent (impossible duplicates by construction), the distinction collapses.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 classifies safe methods as idempotent because a read-only operation repeated produces no additional state change. The hierarchy is: safe \u21d2 idempotent, but idempotent \u21cf safe (PUT is idempotent but not safe). The log's writers occupy the idempotent-but-not-safe cell: they mutate the log, but their mutation is repeatable. The mechanism is conditional append keyed by a content hash or client-side idempotency token; the log stores a fingerprint of prior writes and rejects duplicates at the append boundary. This is idempotence engineered into an unsafe (state-mutating) operation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
